summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Taxa utilize diverse chromosomal sex determination systems: (1) XX-XY (Male Heterogametic: Humans, Drosophila); (2) XX-XO (Male Heterogametic: Grasshoppers, Cockroaches; Henking X-body); (3) ZZ-ZW (Female Heterogametic: Birds, Butterflies); (4) Haplodiploidy (Honeybees: Queen/Workers 2n=32, Drones n=16 developing via parthenogenesis and producing sperm by Mitosis).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 8.1 Chromosomal Sex Determination Taxonomy
1. **XX - XY Mechanism (Male Heterogamety)**: Female produces all identical $X$-bearing eggs ($XX$); male produces $50\%\text{ } X$-bearing and $50\%\text{ } Y$-bearing sperm ($XY$). *(Humans, Drosophila)*.
2. **XX - XO Mechanism (Male Heterogamety)**: Henking (1891) discovered the 'X-body'. Females possess $XX$; males have only one sex chromosome ($XO$), producing $50\%\text{ } X$-bearing sperm and $50\%$ sperm lacking any sex chromosome. *(Grasshoppers, Cockroaches)*.
3. **ZZ - ZW Mechanism (Female Heterogamety)**: Males are homogametic ($ZZ$); females are heterogametic ($ZW$), producing $50\%\text{ } Z$-bearing and $50\%\text{ } W$-bearing ova. *(Birds, Reptiles, Butterflies)*.

### 8.2 Haplodiploidy in Honeybees (*Apis mellifera*)

```
                         HONEYBEE HAPLODIPLOPIDY
                         
          QUEEN (2n = 32)                    DRONE (n = 16)
                 │                                  │
          [Meiosis]                          [MITOSIS]
                 │                                  │
          Eggs (n = 16)                      Sperm (n = 16)
                 │                                  │
        ┌────────┴────────┐                         │
        ▼                 ▼                         │
   Unfertilized        Fertilized ◄─────────────────┘
        │                 │
   [Parthenogenesis]   [Diploid Zygote] (2n = 32)
        │                 │
   DRONES (n=16)       QUEEN / WORKERS (2n=32)
```

- **Unique Drone Genetics**: Drones are haploid ($n = 16$) and produce sperm by **MITOSIS**. Thus, **drones have no father and cannot have sons, but they have a grandfather and can have grandsons!**

conceptBreakdown.heading: Genic Balance Theory in Drosophila (Bridges)
conceptBreakdown.title: Genic Balance Theory in Drosophila (Bridges)
conceptBreakdown.content: Calvin Bridges demonstrated that sex in Drosophila is determined by the ratio of X chromosomes to Autosome sets (X:A ratio); X:A = 1.0 produces normal females, X:A = 0.5 produces normal males, X:A > 1.0 yields metafemales, and 0.5 < X:A < 1.0 yields intersexes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Temperature-Dependent Sex Determination (TSD)
conceptBreakdown.title: Temperature-Dependent Sex Determination (TSD)
conceptBreakdown.content: In non-avian reptiles (alligators, sea turtles), incubation temperature of eggs during a thermosensitive developmental window determines sex: low temperatures yield females in alligators, while warm temperatures yield females in marine turtles.
